  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Driver mobile app", "Location ingest API", "Live map endpoint", "Customer app"],

    "externalServices": ["Device GPS / map tiles"],

    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Anyone who guesses a delivery id can see a driver's live location and phone number",
      "scenario": "The map endpoint is keyed only on a delivery id. An attacker (a customer, or anyone who reaches the endpoint) iterates or guesses delivery ids and receives the live GPS position and personal phone number of drivers on deliveries that are not theirs. Repeated calls every few seconds build a continuous movement trail for many drivers, enabling stalking, harassment or targeted robbery of high-value deliveries.",
      "component": "Live map endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The map endpoint takes a delivery id and returns the driver location and phone number." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "Change the delivery number in the web address and you can watch a different driver and get their phone number.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind the map endpoint to the requesting customer's own delivery",
        "given": "a request to the live map endpoint for a delivery id",
        "when": "the authenticated caller is not the customer or assigned driver for that delivery",
        "then": "the service returns no location or contact data and the request is rejected"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Driver's personal phone number is handed to every customer by default",
      "scenario": "The map response includes the driver's personal phone number alongside their location. Any customer with an active delivery, or anyone who can read the response, permanently captures a driver's personal contact detail and can use it for harassment or to contact the driver outside the platform. Nothing in the design limits this to a masked or proxy number, and the number stays retrievable for the life of the delivery record.",
      "component": "Live map endpoint response",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The map endpoint takes a delivery id and returns the driver location and phone number." },
        { "quote": "Customers see the driver on a live map." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "Customers get the driver's real mobile number, which they can keep and misuse after the delivery.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Never return the driver's real phone number to customers",
        "given": "a customer viewing the live map for their delivery",
        "when": "the response is built",
        "then": "no raw driver phone number is included; contact is only possible through a masked proxy number that expires with the delivery"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Location ingest accepts position reports without proving which driver is reporting",
      "scenario": "Phones post GPS coordinates to the backend but the design does not state that the ingest call is authenticated and bound to the driver's session. An attacker replays or crafts location posts for another driver's id, making the map show a driver somewhere they are not. This can be used to fake proof of delivery, to send a customer to a false meeting point, or to hide a driver's real position.",
      "component": "Location ingest API",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the app does not check who is sending a location, someone can post fake positions for another driver.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and bind every location report",
        "given": "a location report arriving at the ingest API",
        "when": "the report's driver id does not match the authenticated driver session that sent it",
        "then": "the report is rejected and not stored or shown on any map"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Tracking continues outside the active delivery window, exposing drivers' private movements",
      "scenario": "The phone sends GPS every 10 seconds with no stated start or stop condition, and the map endpoint has no stated expiry. Drivers' positions are therefore recorded while they are off shift or at home, and old delivery ids can still be queried after completion. An insider or anyone with a past delivery id can reconstruct where a driver lives and their daily routine.",
      "component": "Driver mobile app and location store",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds." },
        { "quote": "Customers see the driver on a live map." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the app keeps sending location after the drop-off, the company and old customers can see where the driver lives.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit location collection and viewing to the active delivery",
        "given": "a driver with no delivery in progress, or a delivery that has been completed or cancelled",
        "when": "the app reports location or a client queries the map endpoint",
        "then": "reporting is stopped on the device and the map endpoint returns no location for that delivery"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "High-frequency location history is retained indefinitely as a re-identifiable movement database",
      "scenario": "A point every 10 seconds per driver creates a fine-grained trail. With no stated retention limit or aggregation, the store becomes a long-term movement history of identifiable workers tied to phone numbers. A compromised internal account, a misconfigured query tool or a support user can export months of per-driver movement, which is far more damaging than a single live position.",
      "component": "Driver location store",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "Storing a location point every 10 seconds forever builds a detailed map of each driver's life.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Set a short retention period for raw location points",
        "given": "stored raw GPS points for a completed delivery",
        "when": "the defined retention period elapses",
        "then": "the raw points are deleted automatically and only non-identifying aggregates remain"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unbounded 10-second location ingest can be flooded to overwhelm the tracking service",
      "scenario": "Every driver phone posts at a fixed 10-second cadence, so the ingest path is already high volume. An attacker with one driver credential, or a scripted client, posts thousands of reports per second, or a buggy app retries in a tight loop. Without per-driver quotas the ingest tier and location store saturate and live maps stop updating for all customers, so no one can find their driver.",
      "component": "Location ingest API",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "One phone or script sending far more updates than it should could knock out live tracking for everyone.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce a per-driver ingest quota",
        "given": "location reports from a single authenticated driver session",
        "when": "the rate exceeds the expected one report per 10 seconds plus an agreed tolerance",
        "then": "excess reports are discarded and the service keeps serving other drivers' updates"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Falsified GPS from a rooted or mocked device makes the map lie about where the driver is",
      "scenario": "A driver (or someone using their phone) enables a mock-location app and reports coordinates at the customer address while actually being elsewhere, or reports a plausible route to hide a detour. The customer watches a fabricated live map and the business records false delivery evidence, which supports fraudulent 'delivered' claims and disputes that cannot be resolved.",
      "component": "Driver mobile app GPS source",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Delivery drivers’ phones send GPS location every 10 seconds." },
        { "quote": "Customers see the driver on a live map." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "A fake GPS app on the driver's phone can make the map show them at your door when they are not.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Detect and flag implausible or mocked location data",
        "given": "a sequence of location reports for a delivery",
        "when": "the device reports mock-location mode, or positions jump faster than physically possible",
        "then": "the reports are flagged as unverified, excluded from delivery evidence, and surfaced for review"
      }
    }
  ]
}
